deck: Table Rock this morning: 910.43 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Fish the wind.
play.body: Fall bass set up where the shad get blown. A crankbait that bangs is better than a worm that sits.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 910.62 early in the week to 910.43 this morning — about 0.19 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. 1 morning this week the desk had no new gage (carry-forward). Numbers marked “desk” were read from that day’s scout; “carry” was not. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At 910.52 ft, roughly 4.5 ft below full pool, more shoreline, stumps, and hazards are exposed in coves, creek arms, and near some ramps. Boat slowly, especially up the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms, and check launch conditions carefully.

Surface water has cooled into the low 70s with exceptional clarity. Bass are hitting topwaters and soft plastics early before transitioning to jigs, live bait, or drop-shot rigs around long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 feet, and offshore structure. Mixed-bag action includes walleye on points in 20–25 ft and crappie or spotted bass from deeper brush and docks. Clean presentations in this clear, cooling water continue to produce solid catches for those adjusting to the seasonal shift.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~300 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater fed by deep releases from Table Rock stays productive year-round thanks to consistent stocking. Generation remains the primary tactic book: stronger flows favor weighted rigs, drifting seams, and targeting current breaks with 2–4 lb test. Lower windows like this morning allow wading or lighter indicator rigs.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, Gulp eggs, or other soft plastics/scented baits for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many sections. Recent reports highlight improving rainbow numbers, active browns in the upper lake, and productive patterns on marabou jigs, midges, scuds, worms, and eggs. Water clarity is generally excellent. Call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA schedule before heading out.
